description: FIND-001's fix (Phase 3 sprint-2 round-2 review, 'money_safety_gap: gas-seed funds stranded on post-seed failure, no reclaim') shipped as pure code with ZERO corresponding update anywhere in contracts/sprint-2.md, specs/behavioral-spec.md, or specs/verification-architecture.md -- unlike its sibling FIND-002, which received a full 'Correction (2026-07-08, Phase 3 round-2 review FIND-002)' section in the contract (line 201) AND a 'Re-corrected' PROP-303c row update in verification-architecture.md:490. `defaultReclaimSeed` (spawn-orchestrator.mjs:377-406), `attemptSeedReclaim` (spawn-orchestrator.mjs:413-423), and the three wired call sites (identityStep onFailure:613-616, buildChildSpec catch:643-661, mcpStep onFailure:673-678) are real, new, money-moving production code -- a full reversed-direction reuse of scripts/seed-child.py that signs and broadcasts a real Base USDC transfer -- yet: (1) REQ-204's own Edge Cases text (behavioral-spec.md:1853-1868) still only describes the ORIGINAL one-directional gas-seed transfer, with no mention of reclaim/fund-recovery on a later-step failure; (2) REQ-307's own Edge Cases text (behavioral-spec.md:2733-2763), which explicitly enumerates what SHALL happen for 'a failure occurs at step 7, 8, or 9' and 'step 1-6', says nothing about a reclaim attempt anywhere; (3) no PROP obligation anywhere in verification-architecture.md's 118-row proofObligations table (state.json) or its markdown source references 'reclaim' -- confirmed by repo-wide grep (`grep -rn reclaim specs/*.md` returns only unrelated REQ-101/103 LOCK-reclaim hits, e.g. verification-architecture.md:249/439); PROP-204b (line 472) governs only the ORIGINAL seed's SIZING, and PROP-301a (line 484) governs only the INITIATING host's own post-attempt cleanliness, neither covers the child-side stranded-then-reclaimed fund scenario; (4) the contract's own 'Files touched' section (contracts/sprint-2.md:108-124) was never updated to mention this new function pair, unlike PROP-303c's sibling correction which explicitly named its new call sites. This is a genuine asymmetry introduced BY this fix cycle: the SAME Phase-3 gate produced two findings of comparable severity (both 'medium'), FIND-002 got full contract+spec traceability, FIND-001 got none. This project's own established precedent (sprint-1's Phase-3 findings FIND-1901/FIND-1902 each received a new PROP -- PROP-102l and PROP-101l respectively, confirmed present in verification-architecture.md:437 and :802 -- when fixed) makes this omission a deviation from the project's own consistently-applied norm, not merely a stylistic gap. Practical consequence: CRIT-205's own verification-readiness discipline ('every EFFECTFUL call... genuinely exists and is reachable') cannot be checked against this mechanism because no PROP names it as a verification target at all -- there is no criterion anywhere that requires this reclaim mechanism to exist, to be tested, or to survive a future refactor. Note: this finding is about SPEC/CONTRACT TRACEABILITY only -- independent re-verification of the reclaim CODE itself (defaultReclaimSeed's sender/recipient reversal, all 3 call sites firing correctly, original-error preservation, runStep's awaited onFailure not breaking sync callers) found it fully correct and well-tested (skills/self/spawn/lib/__tests__/spawn-orchestrator-reclaim-and-shelter-cost.test.mjs's 7 FIND-001 tests, part of the 195/195 fresh pass this round) -- this is a documentation/governance gap, not a runtime defect.
